draft.title: The five concepts of economics and business
card: The subject is built on five ideas, called concepts. Each one gives a different way to look at an issue.
Resource allocation and decision-making
how people and businesses choose to use limited resources, such as money, time and materials.
Business environment
the conditions around a business that affect how it runs, such as customers, laws and the economy.
Entrepreneurship
spotting an opportunity and taking a risk to start or grow a new idea or business.
Other two
Work and work futures looks at the jobs people do and how work is changing. Consumer and financial literacy is the knowledge to make wise choices about buying and managing money.
draft.remember: Five concepts give five ways to look at any economic or business issue.

a.q: Zoe has $50 and must choose between new shoes and a concert ticket. Which concept is she mainly using?
a.why: Zoe is choosing how to use a limited amount of money, which is resource allocation and decision-making. It is not entrepreneurship, because she is not starting a new idea or business.
a.clue: She has limited money and must choose how to use it.

b.q: Liam sees that no one sells lunch near his school. He starts a small stall and risks some of his savings. Which concept does this best show?
b.why: Liam spots an opportunity and takes a risk to start something new, which is entrepreneurship. Consumer and financial literacy is tempting because money is involved, but it is about making wise buying and money choices, not starting a venture.
b.clue: Look for the opportunity and the risk.

a.q: A bakery has only one oven. It must choose whether to bake more bread or more cakes. Which concept is it mainly using?

a.clue: What limited thing must the bakery decide how to use?
